topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's objectives, historical framework, and foundational concepts regarding the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and deregulated proliferative pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in key signaling cascades confer growth signal independence and resistance to inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how arrests in terminal differentiation drive malignant progression across hematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis, senescence, and cell-autonomous growth limits
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells overcome intrinsic tumor-suppressive fail-safes, including programmed cell death, telomere shortening, and p53 stress responses.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire their energy metabolism through aerobic glycolysis, metabolic enzyme mutations, and epigenetic remodeling.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how developing tumors overcome oxygen diffusion limits by triggering the angiogenic switch to recruit new blood supply.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and barriers of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step metastatic cascade, methods for clinical monitoring, environmental constraints on colonization, and associated genomic features.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a synthesis of the cancer hallmarks and final housekeeping remarks.
